thread:
Alex Kim: Quick Q — FinEdge POC: their vendor risk team asked for our ISO27001 Letter of Applicability / applicability statement. Do we have a one‑pager for hosted-only POCs (hosted API only, no dedicated/private, no customer-managed KMS) they can attach? Need to send today. Thanks.

Emily R: We do have an LoA template. For hosted-only POCs we usually call out specific exclusions. I can draft bullet wording. @Maria Chen any commercial notes (pricing / SLA) we should flag? :+1:

Maria Chen: If they insist on encryption-at-rest with customer keys that's Private deployment (enterprise). For POC we can offer hosted credits and a non-binding prod SLA example, but customer-managed KMS = enterprise addendum. I'll check with Finance whether we need a separate addendum for evidence requests.

Devon Patel: From ISMS mapping, suggest we reference the control domains rather than each control id in the LoA: asset management, operations security, system acquisition/configuration. Draft exclusion phrase I'd use: "Out of scope for this POC: customer-managed key management (KMS/HSM), on-prem / air-gapped deployments, Dedicated GPU pool reservations, and any third-party processors not under Redwood operational control." Also call out retention and logging window.

Alex Kim: Nice. Can you paste the suggested wording we can send directly to FinEdge? They'll attach to their SIG/CAIQ review.

Devon Patel: Sure — paste below. Use as-is or adapt:

```
In-scope for this POC (Redwood hosted environment): Redwood Inference hosted API endpoints for text generation and embeddings; model serving runtime; control plane and telemetry necessary for service operation. Logging and diagnostic data retention for POC purposes: up to 90 days.

Out-of-scope for this POC: customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM), on-premises or VPC-private deployments, Dedicated GPU pools / reserved capacity, backup snapshot encryption under customer-managed keys, and any integrations with external processors not operated by Redwood.

Security evidence and artifacts: Redwood can provide ISO27001 applicability statements, summaries of relevant controls, and pointer to SOC2/ISO evidence on request (contact sec-requests@redwood.com).
```

SecurityBot: Heads-up — internal LoA template here: https://redwood.internal/docs/iso/loa-template-v2 :lock: (access: eng + security). Also uploaded: control-mapping CSV and quick-reference for POC exclusions.

Emily R: I'll tailor Devon's block into the LoA and add a short note on evidence turnaround (3 business days). One question — FinEdge asked whether backup snapshots for hosted service are encrypted with customer keys. We don't support bringing your own keys for hosted today, so we should mark that as "Not Applicable for hosted POC".

Alex Kim: They also pushed on continuity: procurement is asking for a 99.95% SLA for the duration of the POC. We usually don't sign SLAs for trials. Thoughts?

Maria Chen: Standard approach: share our prod SLA as informational only and explicitly label it "non-contractual for POC". If they want a contractual SLA for a POC, escalate to legal and Sales Ops — that typically moves it out of trial terms and may require a paid engagement.

Devon Patel: Add contacts in the LoA for evidence requests and escalation: sec-requests@redwood.com (evidence), legal-sales@redwood.com (SLA escalations), se-team@redwood.com (technical questions). For expedited evidence, note a 3 business day window in the doc.

Alex Kim: Perfect. Emily — can you send the draft to FinEdge and paste it here? I'll follow up with Legal if procurement pushes the SLA.

Emily R: Will send draft and the LoA PDF in ~30m, cc: sec-requests@redwood.com and @SecurityBot for any additional artifacts. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
